atlas-nl.0200: Do not start work on the application receipt alone: the Labour Inspectorate fines up to €8,000 per worker.
atlas-nl.0201: Researcher permit, and PhDs as employees
atlas-nl.0202: A hosting agreement with a university or institute that is a recognised sponsor; no work permit is needed, and you can research elsewhere in the EU for up to 360 days.
atlas-nl.0203: Most Dutch PhD candidates are salaried employees on a four-year contract, entering as researchers or highly skilled migrants, not students; those years count in full towards permanent residence, student years only half.
atlas-nl.0205: The Netherlands has no working-holiday agreement with the UK or the US.
atlas-nl.0206: Only for citizens of Argentina, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Taiwan, Uruguay and Hong Kong aged 18 to 30: one year, not renewable, with casual work.
atlas-nl.0207: Up to 90 days in any 180; no employed work without a TWV. Only nationals exempt from the entry visa (UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand and a few others) can apply for a residence permit after arriving; anyone else who comes as a tourist must go home to apply.
atlas-nl.0209: After five years of legal residence, with the civic integration exam at A2 Dutch and a contract for at least another year at the minimum wage. Years as a researcher, highly skilled migrant or PhD employee count in full, student years half and only for the EU long-term status.
atlas-nl.0211: Recruits from abroad receive 30% of their salary tax-free in 2026, falling to 27% from 2027. You must have lived more than 150 km from the Dutch border for 16 of the previous 24 months, and the employer must apply within four months of your start date to cover you from day one.
atlas-nl.0213: €48,013 a year; €36,497 under 30 with a master’s
atlas-nl.0214: With the housing shortage, check that the lease allows registration at the town hall (“inschrijving mogelijk”) and get the landlord’s signed consent with a copy of their ID: a room without it means a fine of up to €325 and 52% tax withheld from your pay.
atlas-nl.0215: Bring your birth certificate: EU citizens can use the multilingual EU extract, which needs no translation; others need an apostille or legalisation, and a sworn translation unless it is in Dutch, English, French or German.
atlas-nl.0216: Your sponsor (employer or university) files the combined application with the IND. Unless your nationality is exempt (UK, US and a few others are), you then collect the MVV entry visa at the consulate, with biometrics. You cannot switch from a tourist stay in the Netherlands.
atlas-nl.0217: Staying more than 4 months, register in the personal records database (BRP) at your town hall within 5 working days of arriving, with passport, lease and landlord’s consent, and birth certificate.
atlas-nl.0218: Staying under 4 months, register as a non-resident (RNI) instead; since 2026 non-EU citizens can only do so at the Breda or Venlo desks.
atlas-nl.0219: No IND document is required; you may ask for an optional statement that you live here lawfully (€85).
atlas-nl.0220: When the IND writes that your residence document is ready, book an appointment at an IND desk to collect it; if you gave no fingerprints abroad, book a biometrics appointment first.
atlas-nl.0221: Your citizen service number (BSN) is given at the end of the BRP appointment: it is the key to your work contract, tax and health insurance.
atlas-nl.0222: Anyone who works, even a student working one hour a week or a paid intern, must take out basic health insurance (basisverzekering) within 4 months of starting, backdated to the first day: about €145 to €165 a month in 2026, with a €385 yearly excess. Missing it costs a €529.74 fine.
atlas-nl.0223: On a modest income you can claim up to €129 a month of health-care allowance (zorgtoeslag). Register with a GP near home; if all refuse, your insurer must find one within 10 working days.
atlas-nl.0224: Activate DigiD, the state digital ID for the tax office, MijnOverheid, health insurance and the IND, online at digid.nl with your BSN and postcode; the code comes by post within 3 working days, or at once with an NFC check of your passport.
atlas-nl.0225: Never pay a deposit into an anonymous fintech account before viewing the flat and checking the owner in the land registry (Kadaster).
atlas-nl.0226: Do not leave the Netherlands with only an IND receipt or a residence sticker: get a return visa first (€197), or you can be stopped at the border or refused boarding.
atlas-nl.0227: Nationals who must take it have the tuberculosis screening at the municipal health service (GGD) within 3 months of arriving. Students who earn under 50% of their credits in a year can lose the permit.
atlas-nl.0228: Refuse a room where you cannot register at the municipality: without registration your employer withholds 52% of your salary and your bank account can be blocked.
atlas-nl.0229: The IND waiting sticker or receipt is valid only inside the Netherlands: to travel before the card arrives you need a return visa (€197).
atlas-nl.0230: A partner can join only if both of you are at least 21 on the day you apply.
atlas-nl.0231: Since 1 January 2026 non-EU citizens can register as non-residents (to get a BSN for a stay under four months) only in Breda or Venlo.
atlas-nl.0232: Never pay a deposit to an anonymous account before seeing the flat and checking the owner in the land registry (Kadaster).
atlas-nl.0233: For a foreign university near the top-200 line, which year’s ranking the IND uses for the orientation year can be unclear; check with the IND before applying.
atlas-nl.0234: In Amsterdam, Utrecht, Rotterdam, Delft and Eindhoven many rooms are offered without the right to register.
atlas-nl.0235: Bills before parliament would raise naturalisation from five to ten years of residence and the civic integration level from A2 to B1.
